1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
9	
10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry
172

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarKit
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZariskiSep
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZariskiGlueKit
9	
10	/-!
11	# Locally certified divisor families: the `DivFamZar` carrier (DD-2 stage S5b)
12	
13	The Addendum-2 repair of the divisor-functor carrier (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`,
14	Addendum 2): the globally-certified `DivFam` is not a Zariski sheaf — the diagonal
15	divisor over `Γ(C \ pt)` is certifiable on a basic-open cover of the base but carries
16	no global certificate — so the faithful functor value is the **locally certified**
17	quotient `DivFamZar`. The generic germ-regularity engines live in
18	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarKit`.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertified` — the Addendum-2 frozen pin: a span-⊤ family
21	  `g : Fin m → R` with certified divisor families over `Localization.Away (g i)`
22	  divisor-equal to the pulled system; `hreg` is discharged by the Kit's open-immersion
23	  lemma, with the S4 instance provided by `haveI`.
24	* `IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq` — the pin respects divisor equality.
25	* `CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified` — a global certificate is a local one
26	  (trivial cover `g = ![1]`; the certified part is `mapAlg` to `Localization.Away 1`,
27	  whose equations ARE the pulled system on the nose).
28	* `IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — **the mapAlg-hreg
29	  engine**: a locally certified system has regular pulled equations along the
30	  comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'` — regularity is germ-local, each germ
31	  sits over a chart `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` of `R'`, where the
32	  local certificate's regularity transports through its `DivEq` and the landed
33	  certificate-based pullback regularity.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar` — the quotient of locally certified systems by
35	  `DivEq`, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`, `picClass`, and `DivFam.toZar`.
36	
37	Total `DivFamZar.mapAlg` and the Zariski keystones are
38	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg` / `…ZarGlue`.
39	-/
40	
41	set_option autoImplicit false
42	/- Statements mix `Γ(relCurve C R, ·)` with opens produced on the product spelling
43	`(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`; see `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RelativeSectionsLinear`. -/
44	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
45	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161), so the pinned synthesis
46	depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/
47	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
48	
49	universe u
50	
51	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory TopologicalSpace
52	open Opposite
53	
54	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
55	
56	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
57	
58	/-! ## The locally certified pin -/
59	
60	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
61	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
62	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]
63	
64	/-- **The Addendum-2 frozen pin** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): a
65	local-equation system on the relative curve is *locally certified* in degree `n` if
66	some span-⊤ family `g : Fin m → R` carries certified divisor families over the
67	localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` that are divisor-equal to the pulled system.
68	The pullback's regularity hypothesis is discharged once and for all by the Kit's
69	open-immersion lemma — the comparison of an away localization is an open immersion
70	(the S4 instance, provided by `haveI`). -/
71	def IsLocallyCertified (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
72	  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
73	    ∀ i : Fin m,
74	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
75	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
76	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) π n,
77	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
78	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
79	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
80	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))
81	
82	variable {C R π}
83	
84	/-- **The locally certified pin respects divisor equality**: the local `DivEq`s
85	transport through `divEq_pullback` (regularity along the chart immersions is free). -/
86	theorem IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
87	    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
88	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d' := by
89	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
90	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
91	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
92	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
93	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
94	  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
95	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
96	      h _ _)⟩
97	
98	/-- **A global certificate is a local one** (the trivial cover `g = ![1]`): the
99	certified part over `Localization.Away (1 : R)` is `mapAlg` of the family, whose
100	equations are the pulled system on the nose (`pulledEquations` IS the pullback along
101	the comparison; the regularity proofs are proof-irrelevant). -/
102	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified {n : ℕ}
103	    (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : IsLocallyCertified C R π n F.eqns := by
104	  refine ⟨1, fun _ => (1 : R), ?_, fun i => ?_⟩
105	  · have hrange : Set.range (fun _ : Fin 1 => (1 : R)) = {1} := Set.range_const
106	    rw [hrange, Ideal.span_singleton_one]
107	  · haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (1 : R))) :=
108	      isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (1 : R)) 1
109	    exact ⟨F.mapAlg (Localization.Away (1 : R)) n,
110	      Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩
111	
112	/-! ## The mapAlg-hreg engine -/
113	
114	section MapAlgHreg
115	
116	variable {n : ℕ} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
117	variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']

119	/-- **The mapAlg-hreg engine** (S5b): a locally certified system has regular pulled
120	equations along the comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'`. Regularity is
121	germ-local on the curve: the charts `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` cover
122	`relCurve C R'` by open immersions; over each, the composite comparison factors
123	through the certified chart `Localization.Away (g i)`, where the certificate's
124	pullback regularity (`DivisorAdaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors`)
125	transports through the recorded `DivEq`. -/
126	theorem IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
127	    (hloc : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d)
128	    (y z : relCurve C R') (hz : z ∈ (d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) :
129	    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y)
130	        z hz).hom (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y)
131	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) := by
132	  classical
133	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hloc
134	  -- the away charts of `R'` at the pushed cover, and their immersions
135	  haveI himm : ∀ i : ULift.{u} (Fin m),
136	      IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R'
137	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))) := fun i =>
138	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R'
139	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
140	  -- the pushed family spans the unit ideal of `R'`
141	  have hspan' : Ideal.span (Set.range
142	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) = ⊤ := by
143	    have hrange : Set.range (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
144	        = algebraMap R R' '' Set.range g := by
145	      ext x
146	      constructor
147	      · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
148	        exact ⟨g i.down, ⟨i.down, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
149	      · rintro ⟨-, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
150	        exact ⟨⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
151	    rw [hrange, ← Ideal.map_span, hg, Ideal.map_top]
152	  refine Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_immersion_cover
153	    (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => relCurveMap C R'
154	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))
155	    (fun y' => exists_relCurveMap_base_eq C R'
156	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
157	      (fun i => Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) hspan' y')
158	    (relCurveMap C R R') d (fun i ζ => ?_) y z hz
159	  -- over the chart at `g i`: factor the composite through the certified localization
160	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i.down
161	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) :=
162	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i.down)) (g i.down)
163	  -- the away map `Localization.Away (g i) → Localization.Away (φ (g i))` as an
164	  -- algebra tower
165	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away (g i.down))
166	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
167	    (IsLocalization.map (M := Submonoid.powers (g i.down))
168	      (T := Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
169	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R')
170	      (by
171	        rintro x ⟨e, rfl⟩
172	        use e
173	        simp)).toAlgebra
174	  haveI : IsScalarTower R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
175	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
176	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
177	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, IsLocalization.map_comp,
178	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq])
179	  haveI : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (g i.down))
180	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
181	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
182	      rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R (Localization.Away (g i.down)),
183	        ← RingHom.comp_assoc,
184	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
185	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))),
186	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R
187	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))])
188	  -- the comparison triangle through the two factorizations of `C_{T i} → C_R`
189	  have hcomp₁ : relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
190	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
191	      ≫ relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
192	      = relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
193	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := Localization.Away (g i.down))
194	      (R'' := Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
195	  have hcomp₂ : relCurveMap C R' (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
196	      ≫ relCurveMap C R R'
197	      = relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
198	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := R')
199	      (R'' := Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
200	  have step1 := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_congr hcomp₂ d ζ
201	  have step2 := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_comp hcomp₁ d
202	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
203	      (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) d) ζ
204	  have hfinal := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_self_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_divEq
205	    (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
206	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))) hGdiv ζ
207	    (G.adaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
208	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
209	      G.certified.projective_colength ζ ζ
210	      ((G.eqns.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
211	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))).mem_opens ζ))
212	  exact ((step1.trans step2).symm ▸ hfinal)
213	
214	end MapAlgHreg

217	
218	variable (C R π)
219	variable (n : ℕ)
220	
221	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on locally certified systems (Addendum 2's mirror of
222	`divFamSetoid`): the underlying local-equation systems cut the same divisor; the local
223	certificates are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
224	def divFamZarSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
225	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} where
226	  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
227	  iseqv :=
228	    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,
229	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
230	
231	/-- **The locally certified divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`**
232	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): locally certified local-equation systems of
233	degree `n` up to divisor equality. This is the carrier on which the divisor functor is
234	a Zariski sheaf — the globally certified `DivFam` remains the building block. -/
235	def DivFamZar : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarSetoid C R π n)
236	
237	namespace DivFamZar
238	
239	variable {C R π n}
240	
241	/-- The class of a locally certified system. -/
242	def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) :
243	    DivFamZar C R π n :=
244	  Quotient.mk (divFamZarSetoid C R π n) ⟨d, hd⟩
245	
246	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
247	    {h₁ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₁} {h₂ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₂} :
248	    mk d₁ h₁ = mk d₂ h₂ ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ :=
249	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamZarSetoid C R π n)
250	
251	/-- **The Picard class of a locally certified divisor class** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on
252	the quotient by `picClass_eq_of_divEq`. -/
253	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFamZar C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
254	  Quotient.lift
255	    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} =>
256	      d.1.picClass)
257	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
258	
259	@[simp]
260	lemma picClass_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
261	    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) : picClass (mk d hd) = d.picClass :=
262	  rfl
263	
264	end DivFamZar
265	
266	variable {C R π n}
267	
268	/-- **The comparison from the globally certified value**: a certified family is
269	locally certified (trivial cover), and divisor equality is the relation on both
270	sides. Over a field the two notions agree; over a general base `toZar` is the
271	sheafification-of-value comparison. -/
272	def DivFam.toZar : DivFam C R π n → DivFamZar C R π n :=
273	  Quotient.lift
274	    (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n =>
275	      DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified)
276	    (fun _ _ h => DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr h)
277	
278	@[simp]
279	lemma DivFam.toZar_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
280	    (DivFam.mk F).toZar = DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified :=
281	  rfl
282	
283	/-- The Picard class factors through `toZar`. -/
284	@[simp]
285	lemma DivFamZar.picClass_toZar (F : DivFam C R π n) :
286	    F.toZar.picClass = F.picClass := by
287	  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
288	  | h F => rfl
289

8	/-!
9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
10	
11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
17	
18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
19	
20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
30	
31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
32	
33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
40	
41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
42	
43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
67	-/

69	set_option autoImplicit false
70	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

72	universe u
73	
74	open CategoryTheory Opposite
75	
76	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
77	
78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
79	
80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
84	
85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
89	    Type (u + 1) where
90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
101	
102	namespace JacobianData
103	
104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
106	
107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
112	@[implicit_reducible]
113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
115	
116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
121	  d.rep.homEquiv
122	
123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
130	
131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
136	
137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
145	
146	end JacobianData

149	registered)
150	
151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/

164	
165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
166	elaborates with no transport. -/
167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
168	
169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;
170	the group instance must be *keyed* at `Over.mk d.J.hom` (the ascribed `letI` below —
171	instance search does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, but the ascription is pure
172	defeq). -/
173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
174	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
175	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
176	  smooth_of_grpObj d.J.hom
177	
178	/-- Smoke test 3: the unit section of `d.J` is a closed immersion (mathlib's
179	group-scheme instance fires on `d.J` directly, with the datum's group structure in
180	scope). -/
181	example (d : JacobianData C) [GrpObj d.J] : IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left :=
182	  inferInstance
183	
184	end EtaDefeqSmokeTests

10	/-!
11	# DDR-5 — the ε-projection identity (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 5)
12	
13	The projection identity for families constructed from a theta generator seed: the
14	window submodule `K_a(d)` of the DDR-3 family *is* the Grassmannian point the seed was
15	drawn from — `ε` of the constructed family returns the tautological pair.
16	
17	* `LinearMap.injective_of_surjective_of_rankAtStalk_eq` /
18	  `Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq` — **the rank-`g`-quotient surjection
19	  engine** (spec §3 item 5, the equality half): a surjection of finite projective
20	  modules of equal rank at every stalk is an isomorphism (its kernel is finite
21	  projective of rank zero, hence trivial), so nested submodules with same-rank finite
22	  projective quotients coincide.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divisorWindow_eq_of_le`(`_of_isCertified`) — **the window form**:
24	  a Grassmannian point `x` contained in the window submodule `K_a(d)` equals it, once
25	  the Θ-twisted colength module carries its finite/projective/rank-`g` certificate
26	  (`IsCertified.finite/projective/rankAtStalk_thetaGlued`, I-0211) and the evaluation
27	  is surjective (`windowQuotEquiv`).
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorWindow_eq` — **the ε-projection
29	  identity at the seed's window**: for a seed drawn from the point `x` (its submodule
30	  `K = relThetaWindowEquiv '' x`, the W1 spelling), the containment half is DDR-3's
31	  `le_vanishingSubmodule` and the equality half is the rank engine — no fibrewise
32	  input beyond the `IsGenerator` boundary.
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.certifiedFamily` and the ε-forms
34	  `divFamEps_mk_eq_of_le` / `ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamEps_certifiedFamily` — **the
35	  pair identity**: `ε` of a certified family whose windows contain the pair
36	  `(x₁, x₂)` is exactly `(x₁, x₂)` at the pinned ledger exponents `M`, `M + s`.  For
37	  the seed-built family the first containment is automatic; the second-window
38	  containment is the named DDR-5 boundary (fibrewise second-window exactness →
39	  relative, the W2/DDR-4 fan-in; spec §3 item 5 with risk 5's nonreduced guard).
40	
41	The universal instantiation is the G-4 chain (`informal/w4-g4-worksheet.md`), in
42	progress: the tautological pair transported to the pinned window ambients — the seed
43	submodules `K_univ`/`K'_univ` — is LANDED in
44	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeSeedUniv` (with the fibre P-fib-N keystone in
45	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeSeedUnivFibre`); the certificate discharge and the
46	final `DivSchemeEpsUniv` consumer of this file's keystone are the remaining bricks.
47	
48	All statements are conditional on the DDR-3 `IsGenerator` boundary and the DDR-4
49	certificate exactly as `Picard/DivSchemeCertificate*` are — nothing here assumes the
50	unbuilt seed instantiation (I-0210's W2).
51	-/

63	/-! ## The rank-`g`-quotient surjection engine (pure module algebra) -/
64	
65	section RankEngine
66	
67	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
68	
69	/-- **A surjection of finite projective modules of equal rank at every stalk is
70	injective** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 5, the equality mechanism): the projective
71	lifting splits the surjection, so the kernel is a finite projective direct summand
72	whose rank at every stalk is zero — a subsingleton, by
73	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton`. -/
74	theorem LinearMap.injective_of_surjective_of_rankAtStalk_eq
75	    {M N : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R M] [Module R N]
76	    [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Projective R M] [Module.Projective R N]
77	    (φ : M →ₗ[R] N) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ)
78	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
79	      Module.rankAtStalk M p = Module.rankAtStalk N p) :
80	    Function.Injective φ := by
81	  -- a right inverse of `φ` (the projective lifting), and the induced splitting
82	  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := φ.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective (LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr hsurj)
83	  obtain ⟨e, he₁, -⟩ := (LinearMap.exact_subtype_ker_map φ).splitSurjectiveEquiv
84	    (Submodule.injective_subtype (LinearMap.ker φ)) ⟨l, hl⟩
85	  -- the kernel is a finite projective direct summand
86	  haveI : Module.Finite R N := Module.Finite.of_surjective φ hsurj
87	  haveI : Module.Finite R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) :=
88	    Module.Finite.of_surjective
89	      (LinearMap.fst R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) N ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap)
90	      (Prod.fst_surjective.comp e.surjective)
91	  haveI : Module.Projective R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) :=
92	    Module.Projective.of_split (LinearMap.ker φ).subtype
93	      (LinearMap.fst R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) N ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap)
94	      (LinearMap.ext fun x => by
95	        have hx := LinearMap.congr_fun he₁ x
96	        simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, Function.comp_apply] at hx ⊢
97	        rw [hx, e.apply_symm_apply]
98	        rfl)
99	  -- the kernel has rank zero at every stalk
100	  have hker : Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) = 0 := by
101	    funext p
102	    have h1 := congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv e) p
103	    have h2 := congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_prod (R := R) ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) N) p
104	    rw [Pi.add_apply] at h2
105	    have h3 := hrank p
106	    rw [Pi.zero_apply]
107	    omega
108	  haveI : Subsingleton ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) :=
109	    Module.rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton.mp hker
110	  exact LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mp (Submodule.eq_bot_of_subsingleton)
111	
112	/-- **Nested submodules with same-rank finite projective quotients are equal**: the
113	canonical surjection `M ⧸ K₁ → M ⧸ K₂` is injective by the rank engine, so the larger
114	submodule collapses onto the smaller. -/
115	theorem Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq
116	    {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {K₁ K₂ : Submodule R M} (hle : K₁ ≤ K₂)
117	    [Module.Finite R (M ⧸ K₁)] [Module.Projective R (M ⧸ K₁)]
118	    [Module.Projective R (M ⧸ K₂)]
119	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
120	      Module.rankAtStalk (M ⧸ K₁) p = Module.rankAtStalk (M ⧸ K₂) p) :
121	    K₁ = K₂ := by
122	  have hcomap : K₁ ≤ K₂.comap LinearMap.id := hle
123	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (Submodule.mapQ K₁ K₂ LinearMap.id hcomap) := by
124	    intro y
125	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective K₂ y
126	    exact ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk x, rfl⟩
127	  have hinj := LinearMap.injective_of_surjective_of_rankAtStalk_eq _ hsurj hrank
128	  refine le_antisymm hle fun x hx => ?_
129	  have h0 : Submodule.mapQ K₁ K₂ LinearMap.id hcomap (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = 0 := by
130	    rw [Submodule.mapQ_apply, LinearMap.id_apply]
131	    exact (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero K₂).mpr hx
132	  have hx0 : (Submodule.Quotient.mk x : M ⧸ K₁) = 0 := hinj (by rw [h0, map_zero])
133	  exact (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero K₁).mp hx0
134	
135	end RankEngine

152	/-! ## The window form of the projection identity -/
153	
154	section WindowEq
155	
156	variable {a g : ℕ} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
157	
158	set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
159	/-- **The window form of the ε-projection identity** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3
160	item 5, the equality half): a Grassmannian point `x` whose submodule is contained in
161	the window submodule `K_a(d)` *equals* it, given the Θ-twisted colength certificate
162	slots (surjective evaluation + finite projective of constant rank `g`, exactly the
163	`divisorWindowGr` inputs).  Both quotients are then finite projective of rank `g`, and
164	nested submodules with same-rank quotients coincide by the rank engine.
165	
166	`hfin` and `hproj` are consumed by typeclass synthesis as local instances (they carry
167	the `Module.Finite`/`Module.Projective` slots into `Module.Finite.equiv` /
168	`Module.Projective.of_equiv`); the `unusedVariables` linter does not see the `hfin`
169	synthesis and is disabled here for that false positive. -/
170	theorem divisorWindow_eq_of_le (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
171	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
172	    (x : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
173	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
174	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (A.thetaGluedEval a))
175	    (hfin : Module.Finite R (A.ThetaGlued a))
176	    (hproj : Module.Projective R (A.ThetaGlued a))
177	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk (A.ThetaGlued a) p = g)
178	    (hle : x.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow d hH1) :
179	    divisorWindow d hH1 = x.toSubmodule := by
180	  haveI hfinW : Module.Finite R
181	      ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
182	        divisorWindow d hH1) :=
183	    Module.Finite.equiv (windowQuotEquiv A hH1 hsurj).symm
184	  haveI hprojW : Module.Projective R
185	      ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
186	        divisorWindow d hH1) :=
187	    Module.Projective.of_equiv (windowQuotEquiv A hH1 hsurj).symm
188	  refine (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq hle fun p => ?_).symm
189	  rw [x.rankAtStalk_eq p,
190	    congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv (windowQuotEquiv A hH1 hsurj)) p,
191	    hrank p]
192	
193	/-- The window form of the ε-projection identity, with the colength certificate slots
194	discharged from the DD-1 certificate (`IsCertified.finite/projective/rankAtStalk_thetaGlued`,
195	the I-0211 keystones): only the surjectivity of the evaluation remains threaded. -/
196	theorem divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
197	    (hc : A.IsCertified g)
198	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
199	    (x : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
200	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
201	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (A.thetaGluedEval a))
202	    (hle : x.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow d hH1) :
203	    divisorWindow d hH1 = x.toSubmodule :=
204	  divisorWindow_eq_of_le A hH1 x hsurj (hc.finite_thetaGlued a)
205	    (hc.projective_thetaGlued a) (fun p => hc.rankAtStalk_thetaGlued a p) hle
206	
207	end WindowEq
208	
209	/-! ## The seed form: the ε-projection identity at the seed's window -/
210	
211	section SeedEq
212	
213	variable {a g : ℕ} [IsNoetherianRing R]
214	
215	/-- **The ε-projection identity at the seed's window** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3
216	item 5): for a theta generator seed drawn from the Grassmannian point `x` — its
217	submodule `K` is the image of `x` under the window identification, the W1 spelling —
218	the window submodule of the constructed family is exactly `x`.  Containment is DDR-3's
219	`le_vanishingSubmodule` (the landed half); equality is the rank engine on the
220	certificate slots. -/
221	theorem ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorWindow_eq
222	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
223	    (x : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
224	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
225	    (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a
226	      (Submodule.map (relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1).toLinearMap x.toSubmodule))
227	    (hD : D.IsGenerator) (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g)
228	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective ((D.divisorAdaptation hD).thetaGluedEval a)) :
229	    divisorWindow (D.localEquations hD) hH1 = x.toSubmodule :=
230	  divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified (D.divisorAdaptation hD) hc hH1 x hsurj
231	    (Submodule.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp (D.le_vanishingSubmodule hD))
232	
233	variable (g) in
234	/-- **The certified divisor family of a theta generator seed**: the DDR-3
235	local-equation system with its adaptation, bundled with a degree-`g` certificate (the
236	DDR-4 output) into the DD-1 carrier. -/
237	noncomputable def ThetaGeneratorSeed.certifiedFamily
238	    {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)
239	    (hD : D.IsGenerator) (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g) :
240	    CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π g where
241	  eqns := D.localEquations hD
242	  adaptation := D.divisorAdaptation hD
243	  certified := hc
244	
245	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral C.left]
246	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
247	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsDominant π] in
248	@[simp]
249	lemma ThetaGeneratorSeed.certifiedFamily_eqns
250	    {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)
251	    (hD : D.IsGenerator) (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g) :
252	    (D.certifiedFamily g hD hc).eqns = D.localEquations hD :=
253	  rfl
254	
255	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral C.left]
256	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
257	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsDominant π] in
258	@[simp]
259	lemma ThetaGeneratorSeed.certifiedFamily_adaptation
260	    {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)
261	    (hD : D.IsGenerator) (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g) :
262	    (D.certifiedFamily g hD hc).adaptation = D.divisorAdaptation hD :=
263	  rfl
264	
265	end SeedEq

267	/-! ## The pair form: `ε` returns the tautological pair -/
268	
269	section Eps
270	
271	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
272	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
273	variable (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
274	variable {g : ℕ}
275	
276	/-- **The ε-pair identity for a certified family** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3
277	item 5): if the two window submodules of a certified family contain the Grassmannian
278	pair `(x₁, x₂)` at the pinned ledger exponents `M`, `M + s`, then `ε` of the family
279	*is* the pair.  The certificate slots fire from the family's own certificate
280	(I-0211); only the two evaluation surjectivities are threaded (the DD-4 Task-4
281	boundary, discharged by `thetaGluedEval_surjective` under `hfib`). -/
282	theorem divFamEps_mk_eq_of_le (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π g)
283	    (x₁ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
284	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
285	    (x₂ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
286	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
287	        ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
288	    (hsurj₁ : Function.Surjective
289	      (G.adaptation.thetaGluedEval (windowM_choice π hπ g)))
290	    (hsurj₂ : Function.Surjective
291	      (G.adaptation.thetaGluedEval (windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g)))
292	    (hle₁ : x₁.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow G.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g))
293	    (hle₂ : x₂.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow G.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g)) :
294	    divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mk G) = (x₁.toSubmodule, x₂.toSubmodule) := by
295	  rw [divFamEps_mk]
296	  exact Prod.ext
297	    (divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified G.adaptation G.certified
298	      (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g) x₁ hsurj₁ hle₁)
299	    (divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified G.adaptation G.certified
300	      (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g) x₂ hsurj₂ hle₂)
301	
302	variable [IsNoetherianRing R]
303	
304	/-- **THE ε-PROJECTION IDENTITY** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 5): `ε` of the
305	family constructed from a theta generator seed drawn from the Grassmannian point `x₁`
306	at the embedding window `M` is the tautological pair `(x₁, x₂)`.  The first-window
307	containment is DDR-3's `le_vanishingSubmodule`; the second-window containment `hle₂`
308	is the named DDR-5 boundary (fibrewise second-window exactness upgraded to relative
309	divisibility — the W2/DDR-4 fan-in; a fibrewise statement does NOT suffice over
310	nonreduced chart rings, spec risk 5).  The universal carve-pair instantiation is the
311	in-progress G-4 chain rooted at `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeSeedUniv`. -/
312	theorem ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamEps_certifiedFamily
313	    (x₁ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
314	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
315	    (x₂ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
316	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
317	        ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
318	    (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π (windowM_choice π hπ g)
319	      (Submodule.map
320	        (relThetaWindowEquiv C R π (windowM_choice π hπ g)
321	          (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g)).toLinearMap x₁.toSubmodule))
322	    (hD : D.IsGenerator) (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g)
323	    (hsurj₁ : Function.Surjective
324	      ((D.divisorAdaptation hD).thetaGluedEval (windowM_choice π hπ g)))
325	    (hsurj₂ : Function.Surjective
326	      ((D.divisorAdaptation hD).thetaGluedEval
327	        (windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g)))
328	    (hle₂ : x₂.toSubmodule ≤
329	      divisorWindow (D.localEquations hD) (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g)) :
330	    divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mk (D.certifiedFamily g hD hc))
331	      = (x₁.toSubmodule, x₂.toSubmodule) :=
332	  divFamEps_mk_eq_of_le hπ (D.certifiedFamily g hD hc) x₁ x₂ hsurj₁ hsurj₂
333	    (Submodule.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp (D.le_vanishingSubmodule hD)) hle₂
334	
335	end Eps
336	
337	end AlgebraicGeometry

330	  -- STEP 6: back to the Zar classes
331	  have e₀ : (DivFam.mk (G₀.mapAlg B g)).toZar = DivFamZar.mapAlg B g F₀ := by
332	    rw [← DivFam.mapAlg_mk, DivFam.toZar_mapAlg, hZ₀, DivFamZar.mapAlg_comp]
333	  have e₁ : (DivFam.mk (G₁.mapAlg B g)).toZar = DivFamZar.mapAlg B g F₁ := by
334	    rw [← DivFam.mapAlg_mk, DivFam.toZar_mapAlg, hZ₁, DivFamZar.mapAlg_comp]
335	  exact e₀.symm.trans ((congrArg DivFam.toZar hmk).trans e₁)

337	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
338	-- Two `exists_certChartCover` unfoldings plus the away-tower instance block; the
339	-- localization `lift`/`IsScalarTower` synthesis is what costs (I-0227 budget).
340	include hO hχ in
341	/-- **The separation theorem** (w4-ddr9 §2.1, the class side of step 6): two locally
342	certified divisor classes over an affine test that are classified by the SAME morphism
343	are equal.  Together with `isDivRepClassify_unique` — the hom side — the characterizing
344	clause is therefore a *bijective* correspondence on the nose.
345	
346	Proof: the composite certificate × frame cover of each class, refined against the other
347	by the product cover (`span_range_mul_eq_top`); at each common away carrier the two
348	chart presentations of `v` coincide, so `mapAlg_eq_of_certChartFrames` equates the
349	restricted classes; `DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq` globalizes.
350	
351	No certificate over the whole chart ring and no DDR9-U ε-identity is consumed. -/
352	theorem eq_of_isDivRepClassify (F₀ F₁ : DivFamZar C S π g)
353	    {v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
354	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)
355	        (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁
356	        (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm)}
357	    (h₀ : IsDivRepClassify hπ g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀ v)
358	    (h₁ : IsDivRepClassify hπ g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₁ v) : F₀ = F₁ := by
359	  classical
360	  obtain ⟨m₀, c₀, hspan₀, hdata₀⟩ :=

10561	  \leanok
10562	  Let \(F\) be a presheaf on \(\Over(S)\) and \(\widetilde F\) its \(\Sigma\)-extension.
10563	  \begin{enumerate}
10564	  \item (\emph{Amalgamation seam}) For \(g \colon T' \to T\), \(a \colon T \to S\),
10565	    \(b \colon T' \to S\) with \(g \circ a = b\), and elements \(s \in F(T,a)\),
10566	    \(y \in F(T',b)\):
10567	    \(g^{*}\langle a, s\rangle = \langle b, y\rangle\) in \(\widetilde F(T')\) iff
10568	    \(s\) restricts to \(y\) along the slice morphism \((T',b) \to (T,a)\) induced by \(g\).
10569	  \item (\emph{Left-leg rule}) For a slice morphism \(g \colon Z \to (T,a)\) and
10570	    \(x \in F(T,a)\): restriction of \(\langle a, x\rangle\) along the underlying map of
10571	    \(g\) is \(\langle Z_{\mathrm{struct}},\, F(g)^{*}x \rangle\), the honest slice
10572	    restriction on the fibre.
10573	  \item (\emph{Compatibility descent}) If two \(\Sigma\)-elements
10574	    \(\langle a, x\rangle, \langle b, y\rangle\) have equal restrictions along the
10575	    underlying maps of a pair of slice morphisms \(g_a \colon Z \to (T,a)\),
10576	    \(g_b \colon Z' = Z \to (T',b)\), then \(F(g_a)^{*}x = F(g_b)^{*}y\).
10577	  \end{enumerate}
10578	\end{lemma}
10579	\begin{proof}
10580	  \leanok
10581	  (i) After substituting the equality \(g \circ a = b\), both sides live over the same
10582	  structure morphism and the characterisation of equal \(\Sigma\)-elements
10583	  (Definition~\ref{def:sigmaExtension}) reduces the claim to the fibres, where the canonical
10584	  morphism of the reflexive equality acts as the identity. (ii) is (i) applied to the
10585	  compatibility equation of \(g\), using that the induced slice morphism of the left leg
10586	  \emph{is} \(g\) (Definition~\ref{def:mkCongr}, factorisation law). (iii) Combine (ii) on
10587	  both sides: both restrictions are \(\Sigma\)-elements over the structure morphism of
10588	  \(Z\), and equality of \(\Sigma\)-elements over one structure morphism gives equality of
10589	  fibres.
10590	\end{proof}

10592	\begin{theorem}[The \(\Sigma\)-descent of a representation]
10593	  \label{thm:representableBy_overSlice}
10594	  \lean{CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice}
10595	  \uses{def:sigmaExtension, lem:sigmaExtension_seams}
10596	  \leanok
10597	  Let \(F\) be a presheaf on \(\Over(S)\) and suppose the \(\Sigma\)-extension
10598	  \(\widetilde F\) is representable by an object \(J\) of the ambient category, with
10599	  universal element \(\langle u_1, u_2 \rangle \in \widetilde F(J)\) (the image of
10600	  \(\id_J\)). Then \(F\) is representable on the slice by \((J, u_1)\), with universal
10601	  correspondence sending a slice morphism \(g \colon X \to (J,u_1)\) to the slice
10602	  restriction \(F(g)^{*} u_2\).
10603	\end{theorem}
10604	\begin{proof}
10605	  \leanok
10606	  \emph{Injectivity.} If \(F(g)^{*}u_2 = F(g')^{*}u_2\) then, by the left-leg rule
10607	  (Lemma~\ref{lem:sigmaExtension_seams}(ii)), the restrictions of the universal element
10608	  along the underlying maps of \(g\) and \(g'\) are the same \(\Sigma\)-element of
10609	  \(\widetilde F(X_{\mathrm{left}})\); by representability of \(\widetilde F\) the
10610	  underlying maps agree, hence \(g = g'\) (slice morphisms are determined by their
10611	  underlying maps).
10612	
10613	  \emph{Surjectivity.} Given \(\xi \in F(X)\), the \(\Sigma\)-element
10614	  \(\langle X_{\mathrm{struct}}, \xi\rangle\) corresponds under the representation to a map
10615	  \(h \colon X_{\mathrm{left}} \to J\) with
10616	  \(h^{*}\langle u_1, u_2\rangle = \langle X_{\mathrm{struct}}, \xi\rangle\). Comparing
10617	  structure components, \(h \circ u_1 = X_{\mathrm{struct}}\), so \(h\) underlies a slice
10618	  morphism \(g \colon X \to (J, u_1)\); comparing fibres through the amalgamation seam
10619	  (Lemma~\ref{lem:sigmaExtension_seams}(i)) gives \(F(g)^{*}u_2 = \xi\).
10620	
10621	  Compatibility with composition is functoriality of \(F\).
10622	\end{proof}

10641	\begin{theorem}[The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate]
10642	  \label{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf}
10643	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf, AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaSheaf}
10644	  \uses{def:pic0SigmaFunctor, thm:pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover,
10645	    lem:sigmaExtension_seams, def:sigmaExtension}
10646	  \leanok
10647	  The \(\Sigma\)-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is a sheaf for the big Zariski
10648	  topology on schemes.
10649	\end{theorem}
10650	\begin{proof}
10651	  \leanok
10652	  The Zariski pretopology is generated by open covers and is stable under base change, so
10653	  the sheaf condition reduces to elementwise unique amalgamation over an honest open cover
10654	  \((\iota_i \colon U_i \to Y)\) carrying a compatible family
10655	  \(x_i = \langle a_i, \xi_i \rangle\) of \(\Sigma\)-elements.
10656	
10657	  \emph{Structure components.} Compatibility on pullbacks forces the \(a_i\) to agree on
10658	  overlaps, so they glue to a unique \(a_Y \colon Y \to \Spec k\) with
10659	  \(\iota_i \circ a_Y = a_i\) (gluing of scheme morphisms along an open cover).
10660	
10661	  \emph{Fibre components.} The cover members induce slice morphisms
10662	  \((U_i, a_i) \to (Y, a_Y)\) with open-immersion left legs and jointly surjective ranges.
10663	  The fibres \(\xi_i\) are a compatible family on this slice cover: by the compatibility
10664	  descent (Lemma~\ref{lem:sigmaExtension_seams}(iii)), the \(\Sigma\)-level compatibility of
10665	  the \(x_i\) descends to slice-level compatibility of the \(\xi_i\). By the morphism-form
10666	  sheaf property of the degree-zero functor
10667	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover}) the \(\xi_i\) glue to a unique
10668	  degree-zero class \(s\) on \((Y, a_Y)\) restricting to each.
10669	
10670	  \emph{Stitching.} The \(\Sigma\)-element \(\langle a_Y, s\rangle\) restricts to each
10671	  \(x_i\) by the amalgamation seam (Lemma~\ref{lem:sigmaExtension_seams}(i)). Uniqueness:
10672	  the structure component of any amalgamation is determined by gluing of morphisms, and its
10673	  fibre by the separation half of
10674	  Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover}, again through the seam.
10675	\end{proof}

10677	\begin{definition}[Local representability descends to the slice]
10678	  \label{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts}

10700	\label{sec:abelElement}
10701	
10702	For a rational point \(P\) of the curve, the class of the diagonal minus the constant graph
10703	is a degree-zero family on the test \(T = C\) — the element whose image under the universal
10704	correspondence of the representation is the Abel map.

10706	\begin{theorem}[The unit seam at arbitrary tests]
10707	  \label{thm:degAt_relPicToPicEt}
10708	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_relPicToPicEt}
10709	  \uses{def:degAt, thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, thm:picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt,
10710	    thm:degAff_unit, def:relPicToPicEt, def:relPicMap}
10711	  \leanok
10712	  For a test object \(T\), a relative Picard class \(z \in \mathrm{relPic}(C,T)\) and a
10713	  field point \(t \colon \Spec K \to T\), the degree at \(t\) of the unit image of \(z\) is
10714	  the relative degree of the restriction:
10715	  \[
10716	    \deg_t\bigl(\mathrm{relPicToPicEt}(z)\bigr) = \mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\bigl(t^{*} z\bigr).
10717	  \]
10718	\end{theorem}
10719	\begin{proof}
10720	  \leanok
10721	  Naturality of the unit (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt}) collapses the
10722	  restriction along \(t\) to the unit image of \(t^{*}z\) over \(\Spec K\); affine
10723	  consistency (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt}) identifies its affine
10724	  collapse with the plus unit of \(t^{*}z\); the unit normalization of the degree
10725	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:degAff_unit}) reads \(\mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\).
10726	\end{proof}

10728	\begin{definition}[The Abel \v Cech class]
10729	  \label{def:abelCechClass}
10730	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelCechClass, AlgebraicGeometry.abelPicEt}
10731	  \uses{def:graphLocalEquations, def:relPicToPicEt, def:relPic}
10732	  \leanok
10733	  \source{kleiman-picard, abelian-varieties:page-0107}
10734	  Let \(P \colon \mathbf{1} \to C\) be a rational point of the curve (a morphism from the
10735	  unit test). The \emph{Abel \v Cech class} on the test \(T = C\) is
10736	  \[
10737	    \mathcal A_P \;:=\; \struct{C \otimes C}(\Delta) \cdot \struct{C \otimes C}(P \times C)^{-1}
10738	      \;\in\; \Pic(C \otimes C),
10739	  \]
10740	  the graph class of the identity \(\id_C\) (the diagonal) times the inverse graph class of
10741	  the constant point \(C \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) — both factors through the graph
10742	  divisor of Definition~\ref{def:graphLocalEquations}, so one degree certificate serves
10743	  both. The \emph{Abel class} \(\alpha_P \in \mathrm{picEt}(C, C)\) is the unit image of its
10744	  relative class.
10745	\end{definition}

10747	\begin{theorem}[The functor-point formula, \v Cech level]
10748	  \label{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
10749	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
10750	  \uses{def:abelCechClass, thm:graphLocalEquations_base_change}
10751	  \leanok
10752	  For any test \(T\) and any point \(f \colon T \to C\), the pullback of the Abel \v Cech
10753	  class along \(C \lhd f\) is the graph-minus-constant-graph class of \(f\):
10754	  \[
10755	    (C \lhd f)^{*} \mathcal A_P
10756	      = \struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_f)\cdot\struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_{P_T})^{-1},
10757	  \]
10758	  where \(P_T \colon T \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) is the constant point of \(T\).
10759	\end{theorem}
10760	\begin{proof}
10761	  \leanok
10762	  Base change of the graph class (Theorem~\ref{thm:graphLocalEquations_base_change}) sends
10763	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{\id_C})\) to \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{f \circ \id}) = \struct{}(\Gamma_f)\)
10764	  and \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{P_C})\) to \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{f \circ P_C})\); and
10765	  \(f \circ P_C = P_T\) by terminality of the unit test (both factor through
10766	  \(\mathbf 1\)). Pullback is a homomorphism, so the product formula follows.
10767	\end{proof}
10768	
10769	\begin{theorem}[The degree-zero certificate of the Abel class]
10770	  \label{thm:degAt_abelPicEt}
10771	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_abelPicEt}
10772	  \uses{thm:degAt_relPicToPicEt, thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass, thm:classDeg_graphPicClass,
10773	    def:relPicMap, def:relPicDeg, lem:degAt_hom}
10774	  \leanok
10775	  At every field point \(t \colon \Spec K \to C\), the Abel class has degree zero:
10776	  \(\deg_t(\alpha_P) = 0\). The certificate is a proved equality at every point — no
10777	  choice is involved.
10778	\end{theorem}
10779	\begin{proof}
10780	  \leanok
10781	  By the unit seam (Theorem~\ref{thm:degAt_relPicToPicEt}) the degree is
10782	  \(\mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\) of the restriction of the relative Abel class along \(t\), which
10783	  the relative degree reads as \(\deg_{\Pic}\) of the fibre \v Cech class
10784	  (Definition~\ref{def:relPicDeg} on the projected representative,
10785	  Definition~\ref{def:relPicMap}). By the functor-point formula
10786	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}) at \(f := t\), the fibre class is
10787	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_t) \cdot \struct{}(\Gamma_{P_{\Spec K}})^{-1}\) — the ratio of two
10788	  graph classes of \(K\)-points. Each has degree one by the degree-one certificate
10789	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:classDeg_graphPicClass}), so the degree is \(1 - 1 = 0\).
10790	\end{proof}

10792	\begin{definition}[The Abel element]
10793	  \label{def:abelElement}
10794	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement, AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement_coe}
10795	  \uses{def:pic0Subgroup, thm:degAt_abelPicEt, def:abelCechClass}
10796	  \leanok
10797	  \source{kleiman-picard, abelian-varieties:page-0107}
10798	  The \emph{Abel element} is the Abel class as an element of the degree-zero subgroup,
10799	  \[
10800	    \alpha_P \in \mathrm{pic}^0(C, C),
10801	  \]
10802	  membership being the certificate of Theorem~\ref{thm:degAt_abelPicEt}. On points it is the
10803	  family \(t \mapsto [\,\Gamma_t - \Gamma_P\,]\), the divisor-class form \(t \mapsto [t - P]\)
10804	  of the Abel map with base point \(P\).
10805	\end{definition}

10807	\begin{theorem}[The functor-point formula of the Abel element]
10808	  \label{thm:abelElement_map}
10809	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelPicEt_map, AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement_map}
10810	  \uses{def:abelElement, thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass,
10811	    def:pic0Functor, def:relPicMap}
10812	  \leanok
10813	  For any point \(f \colon T \to C\), the restriction of the Abel element along \(f\) is the
10814	  unit image of the graph-minus-constant-graph class of \(f\):
10815	  \[
10816	    f^{*}\alpha_P = \mathrm{relPicToPicEt}\Bigl(\pi\bigl(
10817	      \struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_f)\cdot\struct{C\otimes T}(\Gamma_{P_T})^{-1}\bigr)\Bigr)
10818	    \quad\text{in } \mathrm{pic}^0(C,T).
10819	  \]
10820	\end{theorem}
10821	\begin{proof}
10822	  \leanok
10823	  Naturality of the unit (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt}) commutes the restriction
10824	  into the relative class, where it is the projection of the pullback of the Abel \v Cech
10825	  class (Definition~\ref{def:relPicMap}); conclude by the \v Cech-level functor-point
10826	  formula (Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}).
10827	\end{proof}

10829	\begin{theorem}[The pointing law]
10830	  \label{thm:abelElement_map_point}
10831	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement_map_point}
10832	  \uses{thm:abelElement_map, def:pic0Functor}
10833	  \leanok
10834	  Restriction of the Abel element along the rational point \(P\) itself is trivial:
10835	  \[
10836	    P^{*} \alpha_P = 1 \quad\text{in } \mathrm{pic}^0(C, \mathbf 1).
10837	  \]
10838	\end{theorem}
10839	\begin{proof}
10840	  \leanok
10841	  By the functor-point formula (Theorem~\ref{thm:abelElement_map}) at \(f := P\), the
10842	  restricted class is the unit image of
10843	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_P)\cdot\struct{}(\Gamma_{P_{\mathbf 1}})^{-1}\) on
10844	  \(C \otimes \mathbf 1\). The constant point of the unit test is \(P\) itself
10845	  (terminality: the canonical map \(\mathbf 1 \to \mathbf 1\) is the identity), so the two
10846	  graph factors coincide and the \v Cech class is already \(1\); its unit image is \(1\).
10847	\end{proof}

19	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` with overlap agreement through the clause-transport
20	layer, and the Over packaging by `divSchemeOverHomMk` (F2).

23	  refinement-stable form F6 consumes): over EVERY `k`/`S`-tower test `T` carrying a
24	  certified representative `G` of the restricted class and a pair-chart framing of
25	  `ε (DivFam.mk G)`, the morphism chart-factors.  No localization hypothesis on `T`
26	  — stability under refinement of covers and change of representative is built into

91	    (v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶

93	        (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁

117	the per-piece `divClassify` outputs over the composite certificate × frame cover —

119	`Spec S ⟶ DivScheme g` satisfying the characterizing clause. -/
120	theorem exists_isDivRepClassify (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π g) :
121	    ∃ v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
122	        DivScheme k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)
123	          (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁
124	          (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm),

126	  classical
127	  obtain ⟨m, r, hspan, hdata⟩ :=
128	    DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover hπ g hO hχ r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀

130	  have hv : ∀ p : Fin m,

138	  choose v hvc using hv

142	        ((Scheme.affineOpenCoverOfSpanRangeEqTop
143	          (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover.f q) ≫ v p
144	      = pullback.snd _ _ ≫ v q := fun p q =>

146	      (DivFam.mk (G p)) (DivFam.mk (G q)) (hZ p) (hZ q) (hvc p) (hvc q)

148	    (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover.glueMorphisms v hglue, ?_⟩
149	  intro T _ _ _ _ GT hGT i j ω hω₁ hω₂
150	  refine Scheme.Cover.hom_ext
151	    ((Scheme.affineOpenCoverOfSpanRangeEqTop
152	      (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover.pullback₁
153	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S T))))
154	    _ _ fun p => ?_

158	  exact (pullback_chart_divClassifyClause_compat hπ g hO hχ r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀

163	/-- **Uniqueness / full choice-independence** (w4-ddr9 §2.1 step 6): any two
164	morphisms satisfying the characterizing clause for `F₀` agree — compare over the
165	composite certificate × frame cover (`divScheme_hom_ext` per piece,

168	theorem isDivRepClassify_unique (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π g)
169	    {v v' : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
170	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)
171	        (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁
172	        (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm)}
173	    (hv : IsDivRepClassify hπ g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀ v)
174	    (hv' : IsDivRepClassify hπ g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀ v') : v = v' := by
175	  obtain ⟨m, r, hspan, hdata⟩ :=
176	    DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover hπ g hO hχ r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀
177	  choose G ci cj cw hZ hcw₁ hcw₂ using hdata
178	  refine Scheme.Cover.hom_ext
179	    (Scheme.affineOpenCoverOfSpanRangeEqTop
180	      (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover _ _ fun p => ?_
181	  refine divScheme_hom_ext k _ _ g r₁ r₂ b₁ (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm)
182	    _ _ ?_
183	  have h1 : (Scheme.affineOpenCoverOfSpanRangeEqTop
184	        (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover.f p
185	        ≫ v ≫ divSchemeι k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)
186	          (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁
187	          (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm)
188	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (cw p).toRingHom)
189	          ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ (ci p) (cj p) :=
190	    hv (Localization.Away (r p)) (G p) (hZ p) (ci p) (cj p) (cw p) (hcw₁ p) (hcw₂ p)
191	  have h2 : (Scheme.affineOpenCoverOfSpanRangeEqTop
192	        (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover.f p
193	        ≫ v' ≫ divSchemeι k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)
194	          (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁
195	          (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm)
196	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (cw p).toRingHom)
197	          ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ (ci p) (cj p) :=
198	    hv' (Localization.Away (r p)) (G p) (hZ p) (ci p) (cj p) (cw p) (hcw₁ p) (hcw₂ p)
199	  rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc]
200	  exact h1.trans h2.symm

204	certified divisor class over an affine test classifies to a UNIQUE morphism

206	theorem divClassifyZar (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π g) :
207	    ∃! v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶

234	    (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm) v r hspan

236	      hv (Localization.Away (r p)) (G p) (hZ p) (ci p) (cj p) (cw p)

272	  Over.OverMorphism.ext (isDivRepClassify_unique hπ g hO hχ r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀ hu

10570	    \(x \in F(T,a)\): restriction of \(\langle a, x\rangle\) along the underlying map of

10574	    \(\langle a, x\rangle, \langle b, y\rangle\) have equal restrictions along the
10575	    underlying maps of a pair of slice morphisms \(g_a \colon Z \to (T,a)\),
