10665	  the \(x_i\) descends to slice-level compatibility of the \(\xi_i\). By the morphism-form
10666	  sheaf property of the degree-zero functor
10667	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover}) the \(\xi_i\) glue to a unique
10668	  degree-zero class \(s\) on \((Y, a_Y)\) restricting to each.
10669	
10670	  \emph{Stitching.} The \(\Sigma\)-element \(\langle a_Y, s\rangle\) restricts to each
10671	  \(x_i\) by the amalgamation seam (Lemma~\ref{lem:sigmaExtension_seams}(i)). Uniqueness:
10672	  the structure component of any amalgamation is determined by gluing of morphisms, and its
10673	  fibre by the separation half of
10674	  Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover}, again through the seam.
10675	\end{proof}
10676	
10677	\begin{definition}[Local representability descends to the slice]
10678	  \label{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts}
10679	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts}
10680	  \uses{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf, thm:representableBy_overSlice, def:pic0SigmaFunctor}
10681	  \leanok
10682	  Suppose given a family of schemes \(X_i\) with maps
10683	  \(f_i \colon \mathrm{yoneda}(X_i) \to \widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)\) of big-site sheaves
10684	  which are relatively representable open immersions, jointly Zariski-locally surjective.
10685	  Then the local-representability theorem glues the \(X_i\) into a scheme \(J\)
10686	  representing the \(\Sigma\)-extension, and by \(\Sigma\)-descent
10687	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:representableBy_overSlice}) the set-valued degree-zero Picard functor is
10688	  representable on the slice by \(J\) placed over \(\Spec k\) via the structure component of
10689	  the universal element.
10690	\end{definition}
10691	\begin{proof}
10692	  \leanok
10693	  The local-representability theorem for Zariski sheaves on schemes (mathlib's
10694	  01JJ engine) applies to the sheaf of Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf} and the
10695	  given chart family, producing a representation of the \(\Sigma\)-extension by the glued
10696	  scheme; compose with Theorem~\ref{thm:representableBy_overSlice}.
10697	\end{proof}
10698	
10699	\section{The Abel element}
10700	\label{sec:abelElement}
10701	
10702	For a rational point \(P\) of the curve, the class of the diagonal minus the constant graph
10703	is a degree-zero family on the test \(T = C\) — the element whose image under the universal
10704	correspondence of the representation is the Abel map.
10705	
10706	\begin{theorem}[The unit seam at arbitrary tests]
10707	  \label{thm:degAt_relPicToPicEt}
10708	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_relPicToPicEt}
10709	  \uses{def:degAt, thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, thm:picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt,
10710	    thm:degAff_unit, def:relPicToPicEt, def:relPicMap}
10711	  \leanok
10712	  For a test object \(T\), a relative Picard class \(z \in \mathrm{relPic}(C,T)\) and a
10713	  field point \(t \colon \Spec K \to T\), the degree at \(t\) of the unit image of \(z\) is
10714	  the relative degree of the restriction:
10715	  \[
10716	    \deg_t\bigl(\mathrm{relPicToPicEt}(z)\bigr) = \mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\bigl(t^{*} z\bigr).
10717	  \]
10718	\end{theorem}
10719	\begin{proof}
10720	  \leanok
10721	  Naturality of the unit (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt}) collapses the
10722	  restriction along \(t\) to the unit image of \(t^{*}z\) over \(\Spec K\); affine
10723	  consistency (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt}) identifies its affine
10724	  collapse with the plus unit of \(t^{*}z\); the unit normalization of the degree
10725	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:degAff_unit}) reads \(\mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\).
10726	\end{proof}
10727	
10728	\begin{definition}[The Abel \v Cech class]
10729	  \label{def:abelCechClass}
10730	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelCechClass, AlgebraicGeometry.abelPicEt}
10731	  \uses{def:graphLocalEquations, def:relPicToPicEt, def:relPic}
10732	  \leanok
10733	  \source{kleiman-picard, abelian-varieties:page-0107}
10734	  Let \(P \colon \mathbf{1} \to C\) be a rational point of the curve (a morphism from the
10735	  unit test). The \emph{Abel \v Cech class} on the test \(T = C\) is
10736	  \[
10737	    \mathcal A_P \;:=\; \struct{C \otimes C}(\Delta) \cdot \struct{C \otimes C}(P \times C)^{-1}
10738	      \;\in\; \Pic(C \otimes C),
10739	  \]
10740	  the graph class of the identity \(\id_C\) (the diagonal) times the inverse graph class of
10741	  the constant point \(C \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) — both factors through the graph
10742	  divisor of Definition~\ref{def:graphLocalEquations}, so one degree certificate serves
10743	  both. The \emph{Abel class} \(\alpha_P \in \mathrm{picEt}(C, C)\) is the unit image of its
10744	  relative class.
10745	\end{definition}
10746	
10747	\begin{theorem}[The functor-point formula, \v Cech level]
10748	  \label{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
10749	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
10750	  \uses{def:abelCechClass, thm:graphLocalEquations_base_change}
10751	  \leanok
10752	  For any test \(T\) and any point \(f \colon T \to C\), the pullback of the Abel \v Cech
10753	  class along \(C \lhd f\) is the graph-minus-constant-graph class of \(f\):
10754	  \[
10755	    (C \lhd f)^{*} \mathcal A_P
10756	      = \struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_f)\cdot\struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_{P_T})^{-1},
10757	  \]
10758	  where \(P_T \colon T \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) is the constant point of \(T\).
10759	\end{theorem}
10760	\begin{proof}
10761	  \leanok
10762	  Base change of the graph class (Theorem~\ref{thm:graphLocalEquations_base_change}) sends
10763	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{\id_C})\) to \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{f \circ \id}) = \struct{}(\Gamma_f)\)
10764	  and \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{P_C})\) to \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{f \circ P_C})\); and
10765	  \(f \circ P_C = P_T\) by terminality of the unit test (both factor through
10766	  \(\mathbf 1\)). Pullback is a homomorphism, so the product formula follows.
10767	\end{proof}
10768	
10769	\begin{theorem}[The degree-zero certificate of the Abel class]
10770	  \label{thm:degAt_abelPicEt}
10771	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_abelPicEt}
10772	  \uses{thm:degAt_relPicToPicEt, thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass, thm:classDeg_graphPicClass,
10773	    def:relPicMap, def:relPicDeg, lem:degAt_hom}
10774	  \leanok
10775	  At every field point \(t \colon \Spec K \to C\), the Abel class has degree zero:
10776	  \(\deg_t(\alpha_P) = 0\). The certificate is a proved equality at every point — no
10777	  choice is involved.
10778	\end{theorem}
10779	\begin{proof}
10780	  \leanok
10781	  By the unit seam (Theorem~\ref{thm:degAt_relPicToPicEt}) the degree is
10782	  \(\mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\) of the restriction of the relative Abel class along \(t\), which
10783	  the relative degree reads as \(\deg_{\Pic}\) of the fibre \v Cech class
10784	  (Definition~\ref{def:relPicDeg} on the projected representative,
10785	  Definition~\ref{def:relPicMap}). By the functor-point formula
10786	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}) at \(f := t\), the fibre class is
10787	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_t) \cdot \struct{}(\Gamma_{P_{\Spec K}})^{-1}\) — the ratio of two
10788	  graph classes of \(K\)-points. Each has degree one by the degree-one certificate
10789	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:classDeg_graphPicClass}), so the degree is \(1 - 1 = 0\).
10790	\end{proof}
10791	
10792	\begin{definition}[The Abel element]
10793	  \label{def:abelElement}
10794	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement, AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement_coe}
10795	  \uses{def:pic0Subgroup, thm:degAt_abelPicEt, def:abelCechClass}
10796	  \leanok
10797	  \source{kleiman-picard, abelian-varieties:page-0107}
10798	  The \emph{Abel element} is the Abel class as an element of the degree-zero subgroup,
10799	  \[
10800	    \alpha_P \in \mathrm{pic}^0(C, C),
10801	  \]
10802	  membership being the certificate of Theorem~\ref{thm:degAt_abelPicEt}. On points it is the
10803	  family \(t \mapsto [\,\Gamma_t - \Gamma_P\,]\), the divisor-class form \(t \mapsto [t - P]\)
10804	  of the Abel map with base point \(P\).
10805	\end{definition}
10806	
10807	\begin{theorem}[The functor-point formula of the Abel element]
10808	  \label{thm:abelElement_map}
10809	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelPicEt_map, AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement_map}
10810	  \uses{def:abelElement, thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass,
10811	    def:pic0Functor, def:relPicMap}
10812	  \leanok
10813	  For any point \(f \colon T \to C\), the restriction of the Abel element along \(f\) is the
10814	  unit image of the graph-minus-constant-graph class of \(f\):
10815	  \[
10816	    f^{*}\alpha_P = \mathrm{relPicToPicEt}\Bigl(\pi\bigl(
10817	      \struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_f)\cdot\struct{C\otimes T}(\Gamma_{P_T})^{-1}\bigr)\Bigr)
10818	    \quad\text{in } \mathrm{pic}^0(C,T).
10819	  \]
10820	\end{theorem}
10821	\begin{proof}
10822	  \leanok
10823	  Naturality of the unit (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt}) commutes the restriction
10824	  into the relative class, where it is the projection of the pullback of the Abel \v Cech
10825	  class (Definition~\ref{def:relPicMap}); conclude by the \v Cech-level functor-point
10826	  formula (Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}).
10827	\end{proof}
10828	
10829	\begin{theorem}[The pointing law]
10830	  \label{thm:abelElement_map_point}
10831	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement_map_point}
10832	  \uses{thm:abelElement_map, def:pic0Functor}
10833	  \leanok
10834	  Restriction of the Abel element along the rational point \(P\) itself is trivial:
10835	  \[
10836	    P^{*} \alpha_P = 1 \quad\text{in } \mathrm{pic}^0(C, \mathbf 1).
10837	  \]
10838	\end{theorem}
10839	\begin{proof}
10840	  \leanok
10841	  By the functor-point formula (Theorem~\ref{thm:abelElement_map}) at \(f := P\), the
10842	  restricted class is the unit image of
10843	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_P)\cdot\struct{}(\Gamma_{P_{\mathbf 1}})^{-1}\) on
10844	  \(C \otimes \mathbf 1\). The constant point of the unit test is \(P\) itself
10845	  (terminality: the canonical map \(\mathbf 1 \to \mathbf 1\) is the identity), so the two
10846	  graph factors coincide and the \v Cech class is already \(1\); its unit image is \(1\).
10847	\end{proof}
10848

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
9	
10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry
172

\section{Relative effective divisors}\label{sc:red}

Grothendieck constructed the Picard scheme by taking a suitable family
of effective divisors and forming the quotient modulo linear
equivalence.  This section develops the basic theory of these notions.

\begin{sbs}[Effective divisors] \label{sb:ediv}
 A closed subscheme $D\subset X$ is called an {\it effective (Cartier)
divisor\/} if its ideal $\mc I$ is invertible.  Given an $\mc
O_{\!X}$-module $\mc F$ and   $n\in\bb Z$, set
	$$\mc F(nD):=\mc F\ox\mc I^{\ox -n}.$$

In particular, $\mc O_{\!X}(-D)=\mc I$.  So the inclusion $\mc I\into\mc
O_{\!X}$ yields, via tensor product with $\mc O_{\!X}(D)$, an injection
$\mc O_{\!X}\into \mc O_{\!X}(D)$, which, in turn, corresponds to a
global section of $\mc O_{\!X}(D)$.  This section is not arbitrary since
it corresponds to an injection.  Sections corresponding to injections
are termed {\it regular}.

Conversely, given an arbitrary invertible sheaf $\mc L$ on $X$, let
$\uH^0(X,\mc L)_{\reg}$ denote the subset of $\uH^0(X,\mc L)$ consisting
of the regular sections, those corresponding to injections $\mc
L^{-1}\into\mc O_{\!X}$.  And let $|\mc L|$ denote the set of effective
divisors $D$ such that $\mc O_{\!X}(D)$ is, in some way, isomorphic to $\mc
L$.  For historical reasons, $|\mc L|$ is called the {\it complete
linear system\/} associated to $\mc L$ (but $|\mc L|$ needn't be a $\I P^n$ 
if $X$ isn't integral).
 \end{sbs}

\begin{ex}\label{ex:lsys}
 Under the conditions of (\ref{sb:ediv}), establish a canonical isomorphism
     $$\uH^0(X,\mc L)_{\reg}\big/\uH^0(X,\mc O_{\!X}^*)\risom|\mc L|.$$
  \end{ex}

\begin{dfn}\label{df:red}
 A {\it relative effective divisor\/} on $X/S$ is an effective divisor
$D\subset X$ that is  $S$-flat.
 \end{dfn}

\begin{lem}\label{lm:ctn}
 Let $D\subset X$ be a closed subscheme, $x\in D$ a point, and $s\in S$
its image.  Then the following statements are equivalent:
 \begin{enumerate}
  \item The subscheme $D\subset X$ is a relative effective divisor at
$x$ (that is, in a neighborhood of $x$).
  \item The schemes $X$ and $D$ are $S$-flat at $x$, and the fiber $D_s$
is an effective divisor on $X_s$ at $x$. 
  \item The scheme $X$ is $S$-flat at $x$, and the subscheme $D\subset
X$ is cut out at $x$ by one element that is regular (a nonzerodivisor)
on the fiber $X_s$.
 \end{enumerate}
\end{lem}

\begin{proof} 
 For convenience, set $A:=\mc O_{S,s}$ and denote its residue field by
$k$.  In addition, set $B:=\mc O_{\!X,x}$ and $C:=\mc O_{D,x}$.  Then
$B\ox_A k=\mc O_{\!X_s,x}$.

Assume (i), and let's prove (ii).  By hypothesis, $D$ is an effective
divisor at $x$.  So there is a regular element $b\in B$ that generates
the ideal of $D$.  Multiplication by $b$ defines a short exact sequence
	$$0\to B\to B\to C\to0.$$
 In turn, this sequence induces the following exact sequence:
 $$\Tor^A_1(B,k)\to\Tor^A_1(B,k)\to\Tor^A_1(C,k)\to B\ox k\to B\ox k.$$

By hypothesis, $D$ is $S$-flat at $x$; hence, $\Tor^A_1(C,k)=0$.  So
$B\ox k\to B\ox k$ is injective.  Its image is the ideal of $D_s$.  Thus

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0Functor
7	
8	/-!
9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
10	
11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
17	
18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
19	
20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
30	
31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
32	
33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
40	
41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
42	
43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
67	-/
68	
69	set_option autoImplicit false
70	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
71	
72	universe u
73	
74	open CategoryTheory Opposite
75	
76	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
77	
78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
79	
80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
84	
85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
89	    Type (u + 1) where
90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
101	
102	namespace JacobianData
103	
104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
106	
107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
112	@[implicit_reducible]
113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
115	
116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
121	  d.rep.homEquiv
122	
123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
130	
131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
136	
137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
145	
146	end JacobianData
147	
148	/-! ## η-defeq smoke tests (recon §5 lower-order unknown; `example`-level, nothing
149	registered)
150	
151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/
157	
158	section EtaDefeqSmokeTests
159	
160	open MonObj
161	
162	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
163	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
164	
165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
166	elaborates with no transport. -/
167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
168	
169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;
170	the group instance must be *keyed* at `Over.mk d.J.hom` (the ascribed `letI` below —
171	instance search does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, but the ascription is pure
172	defeq). -/
173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
174	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
175	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
176	  smooth_of_grpObj d.J.hom
177	
178	/-- Smoke test 3: the unit section of `d.J` is a closed immersion (mathlib's
179	group-scheme instance fires on `d.J` directly, with the datum's group structure in
180	scope). -/
181	example (d : JacobianData C) [GrpObj d.J] : IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left :=
182	  inferInstance
183	
184	end EtaDefeqSmokeTests
185	
186	end AlgebraicGeometry

in $B\ox k$ generates $I'$; such a $b$ exists because $D_s$ is an

Consider the short exact sequence

	$$0\to I\to B\to C\to0.$$
%%  \end{equation}
 By hypothesis, $C$ is $A$-flat.  Hence the map $I\ox k\to B\ox k$ is
injective.  Its image is $I'$, which is generated by $b'$.  So the image
of $b$ in $I\ox k$ generates it.  Hence, by Nakayama's lemma, $b$

Assume (iii).  To prove (i), again denote the ideal of $D$ in $B$ by
$I$.  By hypothesis, $I$ is generated by an element $b$ whose image $b'$
in $B\ox k$ is regular.  We have to prove $b$ is regular and $C$ is
$A$-flat.

The exact sequence $0\to I\to B\to C\to0$ yields this one:
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:3a}
  \Tor^A_1(B,k)\to\Tor^A_1(C,k)\to I\ox k\to B\ox k.
  \end{equation}
 The last map is injective for the following reason.  Since $I=Bb$,
multiplication by $b$ induces a surjection $B\to I$, so a surjection
$B\ox k\to I\ox k$.  Consider the composition
	$$B\ox k\to I\ox k\to B\ox k.$$
 It is given by multiplication by $b'$, so is injective because $b'$ is
regular. Hence $B\ox k\risom I\ox k$.  Therefore, $I\ox k\to B\ox k$ is
injective.

By hypothesis, $B$ is $A$-flat.  So $\Tor^A_1(B,k)=0.$ Hence the
exactness of (\ref{eq:3a}) implies $\Tor^A_1(C,k)=0$.  Therefore, by the
local criterion, $C$ is $A$-flat.

Since $B$ and $C$ are $A$-flat and $0\to I\to B\to C\to0$ is exact, also
$I$ is $A$-flat.

Define $K$ by the exact sequence  $0\to K\to B\to I\to0$.  Then the
sequence
	$$0\to K\ox k\to B\ox k\to I\ox k\to0$$
 is exact since $I$ is $A$-flat.  But $B\ox k\risom I\ox k$. Hence $K\ox
k=0$.  Therefore, $K=0$ by Nakayama's lemma.  But $K$ is the kernel of
multiplication by $b$ on $B$.  So $b$ is regular.  Thus (i) holds.
 \end{proof}

\begin{dfn}\label{df:div}
 Define a functor $\Div_{X/S}$ by the formula
    $$\Div_{X/S}(T):=\{\,\text{relative effective divisors $D$
     on $X_T/T$}\,\}.$$
 \end{dfn}

Note $\Div_{X/S}$ is indeed a functor.  Namely, given a relative
effective divisor $D$ on $X_T/T$ and an arbitrary $S$-map $p\:T'\to T$,
we have to see the $T'$-flat closed subscheme $D_{T'}\subset
X_{T'}$ is an effective divisor.  So let $\mc I$ denote the ideal of
$D$.  Since $D$ is $T$-flat, $p_{X_T}^*\mc I$ is equal to the ideal of
$D_{T'}$.  But, since $\mc I$ is invertible, so is $p_{X_T}^*\mc I$.
Thus $D_{T'}$ is a (relative) effective divisor.

\begin{thm}\label{th:repDiv}
 Assume $X/S$ is projective and flat.  Then $\Div_{X/S}$ is
representable by an open subscheme $\IDiv_{X/S}$ of the Hilbert scheme
$\IHilb_{X/S}$.
 \end{thm}

\begin{proof}
 Set $H:=\IHilb_{X/S}$, and let $W\subset X\x H$ be the universal
(closed) subscheme, and $q\:W\to H$ the projection.  Let $V$ denote the
set of points $w\in W$ at which $W$ is an effective divisor. Plainly $V$
is open in $W$.  Set $Z:=q(W-V)$.  Then $Z$ is closed because $q$ is
proper.  Set $U:=H-Z$.  Then $U$ is open, and $q^{-1}U$ is an effective
divisor in $X\x U$.  In fact, since $q$ is flat, $q^{-1}U$ is a relative
effective divisor in $X\x U/U$.

It remains to show that $U$ represents $\Div_{X/S}$.  So let $T$ be an
$S$-scheme, and $D\subset X_T/T$ a relative effective divisor.  By the
universal property of the pair $(H,W)$, there exists a unique map
$g\:T\to H$ such that $g_X^{-1}W=D$.  We have to show that $g$ factors
through $U$.

For each $t\in T$, the fiber $D_t$ is an effective divisor since it is
obtained by base change (or owing to Lemma~\ref{lm:ctn}).  But
$D_t=W_{g(t)}\ox k_t$ where $k_t$ is the residue field of $t$.  So
$W_{g(t)}$ too is a divisor, as a field extension is faithfully flat.
Hence, since $X\x H$ and $W$ are $H$-flat, $W$ is, by
Lemma~\ref{lm:ctn}, a relative effective divisor along the fiber over
$g(t)$.  Therefore, $g(t)\in U$.  So, since $U$ is open, $g$ factors
through $U$.
 \end{proof}

\begin{ex}\label{ex:DivC}

Assume its fibers are curves, that is, of {\it pure} dimension 1.  Given

Show the $\Div_{X/S}^m$ are representable by open and closed subschemes
of finite type $\IDiv_{X/S}^m\subset\IDiv_{X/S}$, which are disjoint and

Let $X_0\subset X$ be the subscheme where $X/S$ is smooth.  Show
$X_0=\IDiv_{X/S}^1$.

Let  $X_0^m$ be the $m$-fold  $S$-fibered product.  Show there is a natural

\begin{rmk}\label{rmk:symprod}
 Consider the map $\alpha$ of Exercise~\ref{ex:DivC}.  Plainly $\alpha$
is compatible with permuting the factors of $X_0^m$.  Hence $\alpha$
factors through the symmetric product $X_0^{(m)}$.  In fact, $\alpha$
induces an isomorphism
	$$X_0^{(m)}\risom \IDiv_{X_0/S}^m.$$
 This isomorphism is treated in detail in \cite[Prp.~6.3.9,
p.~437]{De73} and in outline in \cite[Prp.~3, p.~254]{BLR}.
 \end{rmk}

7653	\section{Divisor classes from local equations}
7654	
7655	An effective Cartier divisor \(D\) on a scheme \(X\) is cut out, near each point, by a single
7656	regular equation. Adapted to the pointed covers of the \v Cech Picard group \(\Pic(X)\) recalled
7657	earlier in this chapter, this data --- one regular section \(f_x\) on each member
7658	of a pointed cover, the sections agreeing up to a unit on overlaps --- is a trivialization of the
7659	invertible sheaf \(\struct X(D)\): on the member \(\mathcal U(x)\) the sheaf is trivialized by
7660	multiplication by \(f_x\). The transition units \(g_{xy} = f_x/f_y \in \struct
7661	X(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times}\) form a unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycle, and its class in
7662	\(\Pic(X)\) is \(\struct X(D)\). This section records that construction and its independence of
7663	the chosen equations up to units; the next builds from it the class of a Weil divisor on a curve.
7664	
7665	\begin{definition}[Local equations for an effective divisor]
7666	  \label{def:localEquations}
7667	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations}
7668	  \leanok
7669	  A system of \emph{local equations} on \(X\), adapted to a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\), consists
7670	  of a section \(f_x \in \struct X(\mathcal U(x))\) on each member, subject to two conditions:
7671	  \begin{itemize}
7672	    \item (regularity) the germ of \(f_x\) at every point \(y \in \mathcal U(x)\) is a
7673	      nonzerodivisor in the stalk \(\struct{X,y}\);
7674	    \item (overlap) for every pair \(x, y\) the restrictions of \(f_x\) and \(f_y\) to the overlap
7675	      \(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y)\) differ by a unit factor: there is a unit \(u \in
7676	      \struct X(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times}\) with \(f_x|_{\cap} = u \cdot
7677	      f_y|_{\cap}\).
7678	  \end{itemize}
7679	\end{definition}
7680	
7681	\begin{lemma}[The transition units]
7682	  \label{lem:localEquations_ratioUnit}
7683	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.ratioUnit,
7684	    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.eqn_restrict_eq,
7685	    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.ratioUnit_unique}
7686	  \uses{def:localEquations}
7687	  \leanok
7688	  For a local-equation system and points \(x, y\) there is a \emph{unique} unit \(g_{xy} \in
7689	  \struct X(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times}\) with \(f_x|_{\cap} = g_{xy} \cdot
7690	  f_y|_{\cap}\) on the overlap; write \(g_{xy} = f_x/f_y\) for the transition unit.
7691	\end{lemma}
7692	\begin{proof}
7693	  \leanok
7694	  Existence is the overlap condition of Definition~\ref{def:localEquations}. For uniqueness, the
7695	  restriction of \(f_y\) to the overlap is again a nonzerodivisor: a section of a sheaf is
7696	  determined by its germs, so it is a nonzerodivisor as soon as each of its germs is, and the germs
7697	  of \(f_y\) are nonzerodivisors by regularity. Hence in the equation \(f_x|_{\cap} = u \cdot
7698	  f_y|_{\cap}\) the right factor \(f_y|_{\cap}\) can be cancelled on the right, determining the unit
7699	  \(u\) uniquely.
7700	\end{proof}
7701	
7702	\begin{lemma}[The cocycle identity of the transition units]
7703	  \label{lem:localEquations_cocycle}
7704	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.ratioUnit_trans}
7705	  \uses{lem:localEquations_ratioUnit}
7706	  \leanok
7707	  On the triple overlap \(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y) \cap \mathcal U(z)\) the transition
7708	  units satisfy \(g_{xy} \cdot g_{yz} = g_{xz}\).
7709	\end{lemma}
7710	\begin{proof}
7711	  \leanok
7712	  Restrict everything to the triple overlap and multiply through by \(f_z\). By the defining
7713	  equation (Lemma~\ref{lem:localEquations_ratioUnit}) applied to the pairs \((y,z)\) and \((x,y)\),
7714	  \[
7715	    g_{xy}\, g_{yz}\, f_z = g_{xy}\, f_y = f_x ,
7716	  \]
7717	  while applied to \((x,z)\) it gives \(g_{xz}\, f_z = f_x\). The restriction of \(f_z\) to the
7718	  triple overlap is a nonzerodivisor (regularity, as in
7719	  Lemma~\ref{lem:localEquations_ratioUnit}), so cancelling it yields \(g_{xy}\, g_{yz} = g_{xz}\).
7720	\end{proof}
7721	
7722	\begin{definition}[The Picard class of a local-equation system]
7723	  \label{def:localEquations_picClass}
7724	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.unitsCocycle,
7725	    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass}
7726	  \uses{def:localEquations, lem:localEquations_ratioUnit, lem:localEquations_cocycle}
7727	  \leanok
7728	  The transition units \(g_{xy}\) of a local-equation system \(d\) form a unit \v Cech
7729	  \(1\)-cocycle on its cover \(\mathcal U\); its class
7730	  \[
7731	    \mathrm{picClass}(d) = [\mathcal U,\, g] \in \Pic(X)
7732	  \]
7733	  is the \emph{Picard class} \(\struct X(D)\) of the effective divisor \(D\) cut out by \(d\).
7734	\end{definition}
7735	\begin{proof}
7736	  \leanok
7737	  Each \(g_{xy}\) is a unit on the double overlap \(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y)\), and the
7738	  cocycle identity \(g_{xy}\, g_{yz} = g_{xz}\) holds on triple overlaps
7739	  (Lemma~\ref{lem:localEquations_cocycle}); this is exactly the data of a unit \v Cech
7740	  \(1\)-cocycle on \(\mathcal U\). Take its class in the colimit \(\Pic(X)\).
7741	\end{proof}
7742	
7743	\begin{lemma}[Independence of the class under unit rescaling]
7744	  \label{lem:localEquations_rescale}
7745	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.rescale,
7746	    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.rescale_ratioUnit,
7747	    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_rescale}
7748	  \uses{def:localEquations, lem:localEquations_ratioUnit, def:localEquations_picClass}
7749	  \leanok
7750	  Let \(d\) be a local-equation system on \(\mathcal U\) and \((v_x)_x\) a family of units
7751	  \(v_x \in \struct X(\mathcal U(x))^{\times}\). Rescaling each equation, \(f'_x = v_x \cdot f_x\),
7752	  is again a local-equation system on \(\mathcal U\), and it has the same Picard class:
7753	  \(\mathrm{picClass}(d\text{ rescaled by }v) = \mathrm{picClass}(d)\). In particular \(\struct
7754	  X(D)\) depends only on the divisor, not on the chosen equations.
7755	\end{lemma}
7756	\begin{proof}
7757	  \leanok
7758	  Each \(v_x \cdot f_x\) is regular --- at every point its germ is the product of a unit germ and a
7759	  nonzerodivisor germ, hence a nonzerodivisor --- and its overlap ratio is the conjugated unit
7760	  \[
7761	    g'_{xy} = (v_x|_{\cap}) \cdot g_{xy} \cdot (v_y|_{\cap})^{-1},
7762	  \]
7763	  so the rescaled data is a local-equation system on the same cover \(\mathcal U\) with transition
7764	  units \(g'\). The rings \(\struct X(U)\) are commutative, so their units form an abelian group;
7765	  hence \(g'_{xy} = (v_x|_{\cap})(v_y|_{\cap})^{-1}\, g_{xy}\), which exhibits \(g'\) as the product
7766	  of \(g\) with the coboundary of the \(0\)-cochain \((v_x)_x\). Cohomologous cocycles on the same
7767	  cover have the same class in \(\Pic(X)\), so \(\mathrm{picClass}\) is unchanged.
7768	\end{proof}

7770	\section{Pullback of a local-equation system}
7771	
7772	A morphism \(f \colon Y \to X\) pulls a local-equation system on \(X\) back to one on \(Y\),
7773	provided the pulled-back equations remain regular; on Picard classes this realizes the pullback of
7774	the associated invertible sheaf, \(f^{*}\struct X(D) = \struct Y(f^{*}D)\).
7775	
7776	\begin{definition}[Pullback of a local-equation system]
7777	  \label{def:localEquations_pullback}
7778	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.pullback,
7779	    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn}
7780	  \uses{def:localEquations, lem:localEquations_ratioUnit}
7781	  \leanok
7782	  Let \(f \colon Y \to X\) be a morphism of schemes and \(E\) a local-equation system on \(X\)
7783	  (\ref{def:localEquations}), adapted to a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\). Pull the cover back
7784	  pointwise: the pulled-back pointed cover \(f^{*}\mathcal U\) assigns to \(y \in Y\) the open
7785	  \(f^{-1}\mathcal U(f(y))\). The \emph{pulled-back equations} are the \(f\)-pullbacks
7786	  \(f^{*}\bigl(f_{f(y)}\bigr) \in \struct Y\bigl(f^{-1}\mathcal U(f(y))\bigr)\) of the equations of
7787	  \(E\).
7788	
7789	  These form a local-equation system \(f^{*}E\) on \(f^{*}\mathcal U\), \emph{under the additional
7790	  hypothesis that the pulled-back equations are regular}: that the germ of \(f^{*}(f_{f(y)})\) at
7791	  every point of its member is a nonzerodivisor. This regularity is not automatic --- pulling a
7792	  nonzerodivisor back along a non-flat morphism can produce a zerodivisor, so the naive claim
7793	  ``pull the equations back and stay a local-equation system'' is false in general, and the
7794	  hypothesis is genuinely required. (Flatness of \(f\) would be a stronger sufficient condition,
7795	  since flat pullback preserves nonzerodivisors; it is not assumed here.)
7796	\end{definition}
7797	\begin{proof}
7798	  \leanok
7799	  Regularity of the pulled-back equations is the added hypothesis. For the overlap condition, fix
7800	  \(y, y'\) and restrict the defining equation
7801	  \(f_{f(y)}|_{\cap} = g_{f(y)f(y')}\cdot f_{f(y')}|_{\cap}\) of \(E\)
7802	  (\ref{lem:localEquations_ratioUnit}) along \(f\). Since pullback of sections is a ring
7803	  homomorphism commuting with restriction, the two pulled-back equations differ on the overlap
7804	  \(f^{-1}\mathcal U(f(y)) \cap f^{-1}\mathcal U(f(y'))\) by the factor
7805	  \(f^{*}\bigl(g_{f(y)f(y')}\bigr)\), the \(f\)-pullback of the transition unit of \(E\). The
7806	  pullback of a unit section is again a unit, so this factor is a unit and the overlap condition
7807	  holds.
7808	\end{proof}
7809	
7810	\begin{lemma}[Transition data of a pullback]
7811	  \label{lem:localEquations_pullback_ratioUnit}
7812	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.pullback_ratioUnit,
7813	    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.pullback_unitsCocycle}
7814	  \uses{def:localEquations_pullback, lem:localEquations_ratioUnit, def:localEquations_picClass}
7815	  \leanok
7816	  The transition units of the pulled-back system \(f^{*}E\) are the \(f\)-pullbacks of those of
7817	  \(E\): for all \(y, y'\),
7818	  \[
7819	    g^{f^{*}E}_{y y'} = f^{*}\bigl(g_{f(y)f(y')}\bigr).
7820	  \]
7821	  Consequently the unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycle of \(f^{*}E\) is the \(f\)-pullback of the cocycle of
7822	  \(E\).
7823	\end{lemma}
7824	\begin{proof}
7825	  \leanok
7826	  The overlap ratio arising in the construction of \(f^{*}E\) (\ref{def:localEquations_pullback})
7827	  is \(f^{*}(g_{f(y)f(y')})\), and the transition unit of \(f^{*}E\) is the unique unit realizing
7828	  that ratio (\ref{lem:localEquations_ratioUnit}); the two therefore agree. Assembling over all
7829	  pairs, the cocycle of \(f^{*}E\) (\ref{def:localEquations_picClass}) is the entry-by-entry
7830	  \(f\)-pullback of the cocycle of \(E\).
7831	\end{proof}
7832	
7833	\begin{theorem}[The Picard class of a pullback is the pullback of the class]
7834	  \label{thm:localEquations_picClass_pullback}
7835	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_pullback}
7836	  \uses{def:localEquations_pullback, def:localEquations_picClass,
7837	    lem:localEquations_pullback_ratioUnit}
7838	  \leanok
7839	  For a morphism \(f \colon Y \to X\) and a local-equation system \(E\) on \(X\) with regular
7840	  pullback, the Picard class of \(f^{*}E\) is the pullback of the class of \(E\):
7841	  \[
7842	    \mathrm{picClass}(f^{*}E) = f^{*}\,\mathrm{picClass}(E) \quad\text{in } \Pic(Y),
7843	  \]
7844	  that is, \(\struct Y(f^{*}D) = f^{*}\struct X(D)\).
7845	\end{theorem}
7846	\begin{proof}
7847	  \leanok
7848	  Both sides are represented on the pulled-back cover \(f^{*}\mathcal U\). The class of \(f^{*}E\)
7849	  is the class of its cocycle (\ref{def:localEquations_picClass}), and that cocycle is the
7850	  \(f\)-pullback of the cocycle of \(E\) (\ref{lem:localEquations_pullback_ratioUnit}); pullback of
7851	  Picard classes is, by definition, induced by pulling cocycles back along \(f\). Hence the class
7852	  of the pulled-back cocycle is the pullback \(f^{*}\) of \(\mathrm{picClass}(E)\).
7853	\end{proof}

  The \emph{fibre Weil divisor} \(F\) is the effective part of \(\mathrm{div}(u)\): the Weil divisor
  (\ref{def:curveDivisor}) with coefficient \(F_x = \max(\mathrm{ord}_x(u), 0)\) at each closed point

\begin{dfn}\label{dfn:Abel}
 The {\it Abel map\/} is the natural map of functors
	$$A_{X/S}(T)\:\Div_{X/S}(T)\to \Pic_{X/S}(T)$$
 defined by sending a relative effective divisor $D$ on $X_T/T$ to the
sheaf $\mc O_{\!X_T}(D)$.  The target $\Pic_{X/S}$ may be replaced by any
of its associated sheaves.  %% And, of course,
 If $\IPic_{X/S}$ exists,
then the term {\it Abel map\/} may refer to the corresponding map of
schemes
	$$\I A_{X/S}\:\IDiv_{X/S}\to\IPic_{X/S}.$$
 \end{dfn}

\begin{ex}\label{ex:PQ-Abel}

\begin{theorem}[Main]
Assume $f : X \to S$ is projective Zariski locally over $S$, and is flat with integral geometric fibers.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Then $\Pic_{X/S}$ exists, is separated and locally of finite type over $S$, and represents $\pPic_{(X/S)(\et)}$.
    \item If also $S$ is Noetherian and $X/S$ is projective, then $\Pic_{X/S}$ is a disjoint union of open subschemes, each an increasing union of open quasi-projective $S$-schemes.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{PROOF.} By [\textbf{EGA G} (0, 4.5.5), p. 106], it is a local matter on $S$ to represent a Zariski sheaf on the category of $S$-schemes. Moreover, it is also a local matter on $S$ to prove that an $S$-scheme is separated and locally of finite type. Hence, in order to prove (1), we may assume $S$ is Noetherian and $X/S$ is projective.

Plainly an $S$-scheme is separated if it is a disjoint union of separated open subschemes, or if it is an increasing union of separated open subschemes. Hence (1) follows from (2).

To prove (2), owing to Yoneda's lemma, we may view the category of schemes as a full subcategory of the category of functors by identifying a scheme $T$ with its functor of points. Denote this functor too by $T$ in order to lighten the notation. And say that the functor is a scheme, as well as that it is representable. Also, set
\[
P := \pPic_{(X/S)(\et)}.
\]
Note $P(T) = \operatorname{Hom}(T, P)$.

Given a polynomial $\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]$, let $P^{\phi} \subset P$ be the \'{e}tale subsheaf associated to the presheaf whose $T$-points are represented by the invertible sheaves $\mathcal{L}$ on $X_T$ such that we have
\begin{equation}\label{4.8.1}
\chi(X_t, \mathcal{L}_t^{-1}(n)) = \phi(n) \text{ for all } t \in T.
\end{equation}
Notice that this presheaf is well defined, because \eqref{4.8.1} remains valid after any base change $p: T' \to T$; indeed, for any $t' \in T'$, for any $i$, and for any $n$, we have
\[
\mathrm{H}^i(X_{t'}, \mathcal{L}_{t'}^{-1}(n)) = \mathrm{H}^i(X_{p(t')}, \mathcal{L}_{p(t')}^{-1}(n)) \otimes_{k_t} k_{t'}
\]
because cohomology commutes with flat base change by [\textbf{Ha83}, Prp. III, 9.3, p. 255]. Hence $P^{\phi} $ is well defined too.

Fix a map $T \to P$, and represent it by means of an \'{e}tale covering $p : T' \to T$ and an invertible sheaf $\mathcal{L}'$ on $X_{T'}$. Consider the subset $T^{\prime\phi} \subset T'$ defined as follows:
\[
T^{\prime\phi} := \{ t' \in T' \mid \chi(X_{t'}, \mathcal{L}_{t'}^{\prime-1}(n)) = \phi(n) \}.
\]
Then $T^{\prime\phi}$ is open by [\textbf{EGA III}$_2$, 7.9.11].

Set $T^{\phi} := p(T^{\prime\phi})$. Then $T^{\phi} \subset T$ is open as $T^{\prime\phi} \subset T'$ is open and $p$ is \'{e}tale. Moreover, $T^{\prime\phi} = p^{-1}(T^{\phi})$. Indeed, let $t' \in p^{-1}(T^{\phi})$. Say $p(t') = p(t'_1)$ where $t'_1 \in T^{\prime\phi}$. Now, there is an \'{e}tale covering $T'' \to T' \times_T T'$ such that the two pullbacks of $\mathcal{L}'$ to $X_{T''}$ are isomorphic. Let $t'' \in T''$ have image $t' \in T'$ under the first map $T'' \to T'$ and have the image $t'_1 \in T'$ under the second map. Then
\[
\chi(X_{t'}, \mathcal{L}_{t'}^{\prime-1}(n)) = \chi(X_{t''}, \mathcal{L}_{t''}^{\prime\prime-1}(n)) = \chi(X_{t'_1}, \mathcal{L}_{t'_1}^{\prime-1}(n)) = \phi(n).
\]
Hence $t' \in T^{\prime\phi}$. Thus $T^{\prime\phi} \supset p^{-1}(T^{\phi})$. Therefore, $T^{\prime\phi} = p^{-1}(T^{\phi})$.

Furthermore, $T^{\phi}$ is (represents) the fiber product of functors $P^{\phi} \times_P T$. Indeed, to see they have the same $R$-points, let $r : R \to T$ be a map; form $R' := R \times_T T'$ and $r' : R' \to T'$. Suppose $r$ factors through $T^{\phi}$. Then $r'$ factors through $T^{\prime\phi}$. So $R' \to T' \to P$ factors through $P^{\phi}$ essentially by definition. Now, $R' \to R$ is an \'{e}tale covering. Hence $R \to T \to P$ factors through $P^{\phi}$ since $P^{\phi}$ is an \'{e}tale sheaf.

Conversely, suppose $R \to T \to P$ factors through $P^{\phi}$. Then $R \to P$ is defined by means of an \'{e}tale covering $R'' \to R$ and an invertible sheaf $\mathcal{L}''$ on $X_{R''}$ such that $\chi(X_u, \mathcal{L}_u^{\prime\prime-1}(n)) = \phi(n)$ for all $u \in R''$. Since both $\mathcal{L}''$ and $\mathcal{L}'$ define $R \to P$, there is an \'{e}tale covering $R''' \to R'' \times_R R'$ such that the pullbacks of $\mathcal{L}''$ and $\mathcal{L}'$ to $X_{R'''}$ are isomorphic. Hence the image of $r' : R' \to T'$ lies in $T^{\prime\phi}$. But the latter is open. Hence $r'$ factors through it. Therefore, $r : R \to T$ factors through $T^{\phi}$. Thus $T^{\phi}$ and $P^{\phi} \times_P T$ have the same $R$-points.

Let $\phi$ vary. Plainly the $T^{\prime\phi}$ are disjoint and cover $T'$. So the $T^{\phi}$ are disjoint and cover $T$. Hence, by a general result [\textbf{EGA G} (0, 4.5.4), p. 103], if the $P^{\phi}$ are (representable by) schemes, then $P$ is their disjoint union. Thus it remains to represent each $P^{\phi}$ by an increasing union of open quasi-projective $S$-schemes.

Fix $\phi$. Given $m \in \mathbb{Z}$, let $P^{\phi}_m \subset P^{\phi}$ be the \'{e}tale subsheaf associated to the presheaf whose $T$-points are represented by the $\mathcal{L}$ on $X_T$ such that, in addition to \eqref{4.8.1}, we have
\begin{equation}\label{4.8.2}
\mathrm{R}^i f_{T*} \mathcal{L}(n) = 0 \text{ for all } i \ge 1 \text{ and } n \ge m.
\end{equation}
Notice that this presheaf is well defined, because \eqref{4.8.2} remains valid after any base change $p: T' \to T$, as is shown next.

First, let's see that \eqref{4.8.2} is equivalent to the following condition:
\begin{equation}\label{4.8.3}
\mathrm{H}^i(X_t, \mathcal{L}_t(n)) = 0 \text{ for all } i \ge 1\text{, all } n \ge m\text{, and all } t \in T.
\end{equation}
Indeed, \eqref{4.8.3} implies \eqref{4.8.2}; in fact, for any given $i, t$ and $n$, if $\mathrm{H}^i(X_t, \mathcal{L}_t(n)) = 0$, then $\mathrm{R}^i f_{T*} (\mathcal{L}(n) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} \mathcal{N})_t = 0$ for all quasi-coherent $\mathcal{N}$ on $T$ by [\textbf{EGA III}$_2$, 7.5.3] or [\textbf{OB72}, Cor. 2.1 p. 68].

Conversely, assume \eqref{4.8.2}. Fix $t$ and $n$. Let's proceed by descending induction on $i$ to prove $\mathrm{H}^i(X_t, \mathcal{L}_t(n))$ vanishes. It vanishes for $i \gg 1$ by Serre's Theorem [\textbf{EGA III}$_1$, 2.2.2]. Suppose it vanishes for some $i \ge 2$. Then $\mathrm{R}^i f_{T*} (\mathcal{L}(n) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} f_T^* \mathcal{N})_t$ vanishes for all quasi-coherent $\mathcal{N}$ on $T$, as just noted. So $\mathrm{R}^{i-1} f_{T*} (\mathcal{L}(n) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} f_T^* \mathcal{N})_t$ is right exact in $\mathcal{N}$ owing to the long exact sequence of higher direct images. Therefore, by general principles, there is a natural isomorphism of functors
\[
\mathrm{R}^{i-1} f_{T*} (\mathcal{L}(n)) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} \mathcal{N}_t \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathrm{R}^{i-1} f_{T*} (\mathcal{L}(n) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} f_T^* \mathcal{N})_t.
\]
Since \eqref{4.8.2} holds, both source and target vanish. Taking $\mathcal{N} := k_t$ yields the vanishing of $\mathrm{H}^{i-1}(X_t, \mathcal{L}_t(n))$. Thus \eqref{4.8.2} implies \eqref{4.8.3}.

7653	\section{Divisor classes from local equations}
7654	
7655	An effective Cartier divisor \(D\) on a scheme \(X\) is cut out, near each point, by a single
7656	regular equation. Adapted to the pointed covers of the \v Cech Picard group \(\Pic(X)\) recalled
7657	earlier in this chapter, this data --- one regular section \(f_x\) on each member
7658	of a pointed cover, the sections agreeing up to a unit on overlaps --- is a trivialization of the
7659	invertible sheaf \(\struct X(D)\): on the member \(\mathcal U(x)\) the sheaf is trivialized by
7660	multiplication by \(f_x\). The transition units \(g_{xy} = f_x/f_y \in \struct
7661	X(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times}\) form a unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycle, and its class in
7662	\(\Pic(X)\) is \(\struct X(D)\). This section records that construction and its independence of
7663	the chosen equations up to units; the next builds from it the class of a Weil divisor on a curve.
7664	
7665	\begin{definition}[Local equations for an effective divisor]
7666	  \label{def:localEquations}
7667	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations}
7668	  \leanok
7669	  A system of \emph{local equations} on \(X\), adapted to a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\), consists
7670	  of a section \(f_x \in \struct X(\mathcal U(x))\) on each member, subject to two conditions:
7671	  \begin{itemize}
7672	    \item (regularity) the germ of \(f_x\) at every point \(y \in \mathcal U(x)\) is a
7673	      nonzerodivisor in the stalk \(\struct{X,y}\);
7674	    \item (overlap) for every pair \(x, y\) the restrictions of \(f_x\) and \(f_y\) to the overlap
7675	      \(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y)\) differ by a unit factor: there is a unit \(u \in
7676	      \struct X(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times}\) with \(f_x|_{\cap} = u \cdot
7677	      f_y|_{\cap}\).
7678	  \end{itemize}
7679	\end{definition}

7773	provided the pulled-back equations remain regular; on Picard classes this realizes the pullback of

\begin{definition}[The fibre Weil divisor]
  \label{def:fiberWeilDivisor}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor, AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_nonneg,

  \leanok
  The \emph{fibre Weil divisor} \(F\) is the effective part of \(\mathrm{div}(u)\): the Weil divisor
  (\ref{def:curveDivisor}) with coefficient \(F_x = \max(\mathrm{ord}_x(u), 0)\) at each closed point
  \(x\). It is effective (\(F \ge 0\)); it vanishes on \(V_1\) (\(F_x = 0\) for \(x \in V_1\)); it
  agrees with \(\mathrm{div}(u)\) on \(V_0\) (\(F_x = \mathrm{ord}_x(u)\) for \(x \in V_0\)); and its
  degree is nonnegative. If moreover some closed point \(x_0 \in V_0\) lies outside \(V_1\) --- a
  point of the fibre over \([1 : 0]\) --- then \(F\) is nonzero and has strictly positive degree.
\end{definition}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  Effectivity is immediate from \(F_x = \max(\mathrm{ord}_x(u), 0) \ge 0\). On \(V_1\) one has
  \(\mathrm{ord}_x(u) \le 0\) (\ref{thm:fiberCoordUnit_order}), so \(F_x = \max(\mathrm{ord}_x(u), 0)
  = 0\); on \(V_0\) one has \(\mathrm{ord}_x(u) \ge 0\), so \(F_x = \mathrm{ord}_x(u)\). The degree
  \(\deg_K F = \sum_x F_x\,[\kappa(x):K]\) (\ref{def:curveDivisor_deg}) is a finite sum of
  nonnegative terms, each \(F_x \ge 0\) and each residue degree nonnegative, hence \(\deg_K F \ge 0\).
  Given a witness \(x_0 \in V_0 \setminus V_1\): there \(F_{x_0} = \mathrm{ord}_{x_0}(u) \ge 1\)
  (\ref{thm:fiberCoordUnit_order}), so \(F \ne 0\); and the degree, again a sum of nonnegative terms,
  is bounded below by the single term \(F_{x_0}\,[\kappa(x_0):K] \ge 1\cdot[\kappa(x_0):K] > 0\),
  using positivity of the residue degree (\ref{thm:residueDeg_pos}). Hence \(\deg_K F > 0\).
\end{proof}
